issues.summary: Contact damage never lands: DK overlaps the first Gnawty for 3800+ frames unharmed in BOTH native and wide modes, and identically under forced LLE (not a dispatch/widescreen defect).
issues.expected: Verify against emulator ground truth first; if stock damages a standing DK here, suspect the recomp collision path.
issues.fixed_note: verified fixed 2026-08-16: on the current build the death route takes both hits and the two-Kong death fires at frame ~7711 (world teardown, $0028 reset, Kong counter decrement), landing on the post-death map. Fixed upstream by the concurrent runtime/dispatch work; damage-chain map for future reference: contact probe (BBA574/BBA58D, touched slot in $88/$16F5) -> event $40 in SprEventFlags $1595+slot -> Player_HandleHitEvents $BFA0F7 (consumes same frame; end-of-frame dumps never show the flag) -> state $19 + invuln $C0.

issues.summary: WIDE<->CENTERED presentation flap during level entry (frames 7304-7331 of the jungle route).
issues.expected: Single clean transition to EXTEND once bounds/calibration are ready.

issues.summary: Wide world key camX=$FFF0 (-16) unwrap artifact near level start.
issues.expected: World keys clamp at the level's west bound instead of unwrapping.

issues.summary: Stream retrodiction proves 1690 served-margin entries on the jungle entry route disagree with the game's own later stream, overwhelmingly in the ATTRIBUTE byte (palette/priority/flip: xor 0x1c00/0x5c00/0x4c00 clusters; whole 29-row columns as they scroll into view). The ROM level-map decoder's attribute derivation does not match streamed truth for some metatiles - margins can show wrong-palette art.
issues.fixed_note: fixed 2026-08-16 by the margin decode/localization rework; retrodiction now reports zero mismatches on the jungle route; contract ratchet tightened to 0

issues.summary: At level entry (~frame 7488) an OAM sprite drops its X high bit: (317,158) -> (69,158) with the low byte continuous - right-margin art teleporting to the left. Caught by level_sweep's wrap detector; likely tied to the entry-time presentation-bias window (see entry-wide-centered-flap / wide-world-key-unwrap).
issues.expected: Sprites keep the 9-bit X across the entry transition; zero wrap_suspects in the sweep.

issues.summary: Standing still at level start pillarboxes for 4000+ frames (layout never selected, source bank 0) until the camera moves; seen on route_death.dks stand-still segment.
issues.expected: Calibration should lock from the entry decode without requiring camera motion.

issues.summary: Leaving a bonus room could seed BG1 widescreen margins from a transitional VRAM ring, producing repeated vertical strips on both outer edges while the native center and cartridge state remained valid.
issues.expected: Unknown-layout stream coverage is rejected until calibration establishes a real layout; the repaired retained render equals a cold reconstruction without changing gameplay timing.
issues.fixed_note: fixed 2026-08-16; first visible divergence was relative frame 307, three 464-frame replays are byte-identical, and the final retained/cold left-center-right comparison is exact

issues.summary: Wide simultaneous horizontal/vertical motion could expose black or mixed-color rectangular blocks in BG1 because the stock vertical row builder refreshed only 36 entries before publishing a full 64-entry ring row.
issues.expected: Both authentic vertical row builders execute two overlapping stock passes in eligible wide gameplay, restore Layer1X exactly, and keep the native path unchanged.
issues.fixed_note: fixed 2026-08-16; the 809-frame raw-BG1 zero groups now match the native oracle, the later 3559-frame route is clean and byte-identical across three repeats, and the seven-sample retained/cold transition sentinel passes

issues.summary: The host renderer sampled seven complete margin tiles at arbitrary sub-tile scroll phases, but the cartridge initializer and moving-row sweep prepared only six. The uninitialized seventh physical BG1 ring column could later rotate into the native center as one 8-pixel vertical strip of stale terrain.
issues.expected: Cartridge initialization and moving-row coverage include the same seven tile columns consumed by the renderer; post-corruption save states remain historical evidence and are not treated as fresh-entry proof.
issues.fixed_note: fixed 2026-08-16 first by restoring the 56-pixel experimental cartridge contract, then superseded by the safer stock-cartridge default after cross-level fresh-entry testing proved the widened initializer itself corrupts some layouts. Host ROM prefill plus stock streaming retains the accepted 809-frame and 3559-frame Jungle framebuffer hashes; the widened path is now research-only.

issues.summary: Jungle Hijinxs Bonus 1 lost its purple floor and showed checkerboard cave columns because a shared fixed-layout initializer was incorrectly treated as a rolling-terrain widescreen capability and wrote widened columns into the native VRAM ring.
issues.expected: Mode $0001, level $0009, entrance $0006 keeps the cartridge initializer stock; the host handles only the side presentation, and a fresh route renders the complete cave floor without changing ordinary scrolling terrain.
issues.fixed_note: fixed 2026-08-16 by making stock cartridge initialization/row streaming the global fail-closed default; the old widening is research-only behind DKC1_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_CARTRIDGE_WIDENING=1. Three 3589-frame fresh-entry replays restore the cave floor, while a separate authentic Ropey Rampage A/B proves the same containment restores its full terrain. Binaries from 05:44 through the pre-rowfix 08:11 build reproduce the old corruption, locating the broad policy to commit 6bf8981 rather than the later seven-tile change.

issues.summary: Ropey Rampage could start with terrain sliced into displaced horizontal and vertical bands because the shared widened cartridge initializer generated invalid native-ring data for this layout.
issues.expected: An authentic Ropey Rampage entry uses stock cartridge initialization and renders a continuous floor/background across the 16:9 frame; center correctness is checked against raw/native evidence rather than margin availability alone.
issues.fixed_note: fixed 2026-08-16 by globally failing closed to stock cartridge initialization/row streaming. The authentic 601-frame entry is clean and byte-identical across three runs (frame b894ba8b..., WRAM 5748eb98..., VRAM 80476dd3...). The widened A/B deterministically reproduces the sliced terrain.

issues.summary: Underwater level $0061/$80BF stayed entirely 4:3 because the host decoded both level-map cells and metatile definitions from the map bank. This scene publishes map bank $E9 in $D5 and metatile-definition bank $D0 in $D6, so the one-bank decode failed calibration and correctly fell back to pillarbox.
issues.expected: ROM level decoding reads map cells from $D5 and metatile definitions from $D6, includes both banks in source identity/trace evidence, and widens only after the native rolling tilemap calibration passes.
issues.fixed_note: fixed 2026-08-16 by splitting the decoder inputs. The exact state improved vertical calibration from 50/224 to 212/224, selected the vertical layout, and rendered real terrain on both sides. Three independent 120-frame candidate replays are byte-identical (frame 54d5958e..., WRAM abf22673..., VRAM 24481010...).

issues.summary: Croctopus Chase level $0061/$00BF widened correctly, but its lower-right rock wall stopped at the native edge and exposed BG2 water in the right margin. The ROM map itself switches from a fully populated wall metatile at world X $0620-$063F to wholly transparent metatiles at X $0640 because those cells were never visible on stock hardware.
issues.expected: Only wholly transparent 32x32 metatiles beyond the native right edge continue the nearest fully populated wall boundary. Native pixels, cartridge memory, partial openings, and every other level remain unchanged.
issues.fixed_note: fixed 2026-08-16 with a scene-locked, presentation-only vertical-boundary continuation. The exact frame replaces 96 transparent margin tiles; WRAM, VRAM, CGRAM, and both OAM copies remain byte-identical. The 256px native center matches its oracle at all 57,344 pixels, three frame captures are byte-identical (SHA-256 AAB0EF0B...), and three 3,551-frame input-history replays end at exact WRAM F5BCA064....

issues.summary: At Croctopus Chase level $0061/$00C0 near camera X $007F, BG1's first offscreen right metatile was a complete wall but the following unused metatile was empty. The continuation rule skipped the nearer complete block and tested only the native-edge block, leaving alternating water and rock fragments in the outermost right margin.
issues.expected: An empty right-margin metatile continues from the nearest fully populated metatile back toward the native viewport. The accepted left-boundary behavior, all native pixels, cartridge memory, partial openings, and other scenes remain unchanged.
issues.fixed_note: fixed 2026-08-16 by searching inward only on the right for the nearest complete continuation source. The exact frame continues 93 tiles and changes 1,491 pixels, all in the 43-pixel right margin; the native center and every other plane are exact. Both previously fixed Croctopus boundary states are pixel-identical, native 4:3 is byte-identical on all five captured surfaces, and three candidate composites are byte-identical (SHA-256 0FDA2212...).

issues.summary: At world X $0241 in Croctopus Chase level $0061/$00BF, BG1's rock wall stopped 11 pixels inside the left widescreen margin and exposed BG2 water. The ROM map has a fully populated wall metatile at the stock left edge (metatile X $12) but a wholly transparent offscreen metatile at X $10.
issues.expected: The same scene-locked margin continuation used on the right applies symmetrically: only wholly transparent metatiles beyond either native lateral edge may reuse the nearest fully populated wall boundary. Native pixels, cartridge memory, partial openings, and every other level remain unchanged.
issues.fixed_note: fixed 2026-08-16 by generalizing the guarded underwater boundary rule to both margins. The exact frame continues 93 presentation tiles and changes 2,357 pixels, all within the outermost 11 pixels of the left margin; center and right are byte-identical. The 57,344-pixel native center is exact, WRAM/VRAM remain exact, and three independent captures are byte-identical (SHA-256 96B1D386...).
